week_headline: Thyroid supplements surge in popularity as people seek metabolic shortcuts for weight loss

top10.claim: Do Thyroid Supplements Help With Weight Loss ?
top10.verdict: For the vast majority of people, thyroid supplements do not help with weight loss and can actually be harmful. If your thyroid is functioning normally, adding iodine, selenium, or other thyroid-support ingredients won't speed up your metabolism — your body simply doesn't work that way. Only people with a confirmed, medically diagnosed thyroid condition see weight changes through proper treatment, and even then, thyroid medication is prescribed by a doctor, not bought off a shelf.
top10.verdict_highlight: Normal thyroids don't benefit from supplements
sources: American Thyroid Association (ATA) — thyroid and weight position statement
JAMA Internal Medicine — over-the-counter thyroid supplements study, 2013
NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — iodine and thyroid function fact sheet
top10.global_opinion: In the US, thyroid supplements are loosely regulated as dietary supplements under FDA rules, meaning companies can market them without proving efficacy — this has fuelled explosive growth in the category. The EU and UK take a stricter stance, with the MHRA and EFSA requiring more evidence before health claims appear on labels, making these products less prevalent in European pharmacies. In Australia, the TGA similarly regulates thyroid support products as complementary medicines, requiring listed ingredients to be safe but not necessarily proven effective for weight loss.
top10.brit_take: In the UK we'd probably just be told to have a cup of tea and get a proper blood test from your GP before spending £40 on a bottle of kelp tablets.
